Pita Baker's Percentage

Roll thin disks and bake them very hot so they balloon into a pocket. A crowded oven will not puff them.

Detailed method

The calculator opens at 400 g flour, 62% hydration, 1.8% salt, and 0.7% yeast. The balls fields open at 8 disks of about 82 g. Roll them thin and bake them very hot so they puff. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Mix Stir the flour, water, salt, and yeast, then knead about 6 minutes until smooth. At 62% hydration the dough is soft, not slack. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  2. Bulk Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for 60 to 90 minutes. With 0.7% yeast it should nearly double.
  3. Divide Divide into eight pieces of about 82 g. Roll each into a smooth ball, cover, and rest 15 to 20 minutes.
  4. Roll Dust the counter lightly. Roll each ball to about 15 cm across and about 0.5 cm thick. A tear in the skin will not puff.
  5. Heat Heat a stone, steel, or an inverted heavy sheet at 250°C (480°F) for 30 minutes. Cover the disks while you wait.
  6. Bake Bake one or two at a time for 2 to 4 minutes, until they balloon. If they stay flat, the oven is too cool or the disk is too thick.
  7. Stack As they come out, stack them in a towel so the crust stays soft. The pocket is the space that opened inside.
